tutorial.title: Python Dependencies
tutorial.descriptionContent: Recall and apply package installation, requirements, and version rules through interleaved practice.
tutorial.shortDescriptionContent: Python learners who completed tutorials 4603 and 4604

lessons.title: Find the Standard Module
lessons.interactiveContent:
Which module comes with Python's standard library?

mathtabulaterequests

Make sure to pick math.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Your program imports math and tabulate. In a fresh Python environment, which one needs a third-party installation?

tabulate only; math comes with Python.math only; tabulate comes with Python.Both, because every import requires a separate installation.

tabulate only; math comes with Python.

lessons.title: Spot the Version Risk
lessons.interactiveContent:
Which kind of package release can require changes to an older project's code?

A release with a breaking changeThe same release the project already usesA release that changes only its documentation

A release with a breaking change.
lessons.hardModeContent:
A new package release removes a function your project calls. What can happen if you update without changing that call?

The old call can stop working because the function is no longer available.The call must keep working because the package name did not change.Python automatically rewrites the call to a replacement function.

The old call can stop working because the function is no longer available.

lessons.title: Complete the pip Command
lessons.interactiveContent:
Complete the action that adds tabulate to the active environment.

Make sure to pick install.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Complete the action that adds tabulate to the active environment.

Make sure to pick pip, followed by install, and finally tabulate.

lessons.title: Read the Exact Pin
lessons.interactiveContent:
Which exact version does this requirement install?

0.8.100.8Any version newer than 0.8.10

Make sure to pick 0.8.10.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Version 0.9.0 is released. You keep this file unchanged and install from it in a fresh environment. Can pip choose the new release?

No, the exact pin still requires 0.8.10.Yes, pip always replaces an older pin with the newest release.Yes, the pin accepts every release with a version starting with 0.

No, the exact pin still requires 0.8.10.

lessons.title: Diagnose the Missing Package
lessons.interactiveContent:
A third-party import raises ModuleNotFoundError. What should happen before the next import attempt?

Install the missing package in the environmentRepeat the same import without changesRemove Python's standard library

Install the missing package in the environment.
lessons.hardModeContent:
import tabulate raises ModuleNotFoundError because it is not installed. Which change addresses the cause?

Run pip install tabulate in the active environment, then retry the import.Change import tabulate to from tabulate import tabulate without installing.Run pip install math, then retry import tabulate.

Run pip install tabulate in the active environment, then retry the import.

lessons.title: Complete the Exact Pin
lessons.interactiveContent:
Complete the operator that pins requests to one exact version.

Make sure to pick ==.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Complete the operator that pins requests to one exact version.

Make sure to pick requests, followed by ==, and finally 2.32.3.

lessons.title: Recognize the Environment
lessons.interactiveContent:
A third-party package is installed in one isolated Python environment. What must a separate isolated environment do before importing it?

Install the package in the separate environmentAssume the environments share installed packagesRename the package as a standard module

Install the package in the separate environment.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Environment A has the package installed. You copy requirements.txt into separate environment B. Can B import it just from that copy?

No; install the listed package in B first.Yes; the requirements file itself contains the installed package.Yes; B automatically uses the package installed in A.

No; install the listed package in B first.

lessons.title: Read the Lower Bound
lessons.interactiveContent:
Which versions can this lower bound accept?

Version 2.30 and newer versionsOnly version 2.30Versions below 2.30

Version 2.30 and newer versions.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Which versions can this lower bound accept?

Version 2.30 and newer versionsOnly version 2.30Only releases newer than version 2.30

Version 2.30 and newer versions.

lessons.title: Identify a Dependency
lessons.interactiveContent:
What is a dependency in requirements.txt?

A third-party package the project needsEvery standard-library module Python includesA command that imports Python code

A third-party package the project needs.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Your project needs the third-party package tabulate. Which line records that dependency in requirements.txt?

tabulateimport tabulatepip install tabulate

Make sure to pick tabulate.

lessons.title: List the Project Dependencies
lessons.interactiveContent:
A project imports the standard-library module math and the third-party packages tabulate and requests. Which requirements file is correct?

tabulaterequestsmathtabulaterequestsmath

Make sure to pick tabulaterequests.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Your project uses standard-library math plus third-party tabulate and requests.

It stops using requests and now needs third-party numpy. Which file lists the current dependencies, one per line?

tabulate
numpymath
tabulate
numpytabulate
requests

Make sure to pick tabulate
numpy.

lessons.title: Complete the Upper Bound
lessons.interactiveContent:
Complete the operator that excludes version 3 and anything newer.

Make sure to pick <.

lessons.title: Install the Requirements
lessons.interactiveContent:
Complete the option that tells pip to read dependencies from a file.

Make sure to pick -r.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Complete the option that tells pip to read dependencies from a file.

Make sure to pick pip, followed by install, and finally -r.

lessons.title: Interpret the Version Range
lessons.interactiveContent:
Which statement matches this bounded range?

Use version 0.8 or newer, but stay below 1Use only version 0.8Use version 1 or newer

Use version 0.8 or newer, but stay below 1.
lessons.hardModeContent:
A release 0.9 becomes available while 1 is also available. With this file unchanged, which release does the range permit?

0.9 is permitted; 1 is excluded.Both 0.9 and 1 are permitted.Neither is permitted because the file allows only 0.8.

0.9 is permitted; 1 is excluded.

lessons.title: Choose the Standard Filename
lessons.interactiveContent:
Which standard filename records a Python project's dependencies?

requirements.txtimports.pypackages.command

Make sure to pick requirements.txt.
lessons.hardModeContent:
You save the package list under the standard Python requirements filename. Which command installs the packages from that file?

pip install -r requirements.txtpip install requirements.txtimport requirements.txt

pip install -r requirements.txt.

lessons.title: Choose a Version Strategy
lessons.interactiveContent:
A team must reproduce one tested release exactly. Which requirement fits that goal?

tabulate==0.8.10tabulate>=0.8tabulate<1

Make sure to pick tabulate==0.8.10.
lessons.hardModeContent:
You currently use tabulate>=0.8. You now need exactly the tested 0.8.10 release. Which replacement guarantees that request?

tabulate==0.8.10tabulate>=0.8.10tabulate<=0.8.10

Make sure to pick tabulate==0.8.10.

lessons.title: Order Installation and Import
lessons.interactiveContent:
A new environment doesn't have a required third-party package yet. Which sequence prepares the program to use it?

Install the package, then import itImport the package, then install itImport the package without adding it to the environment

Install the package, then import it.
lessons.hardModeContent:
You successfully installed tabulate in the active environment. Which next step makes it available by name inside script.py?

Add import tabulate to script.py.Write pip install tabulate as Python code inside script.py.Use tabulate in script.py without importing because installation defines the name.

Add import tabulate to script.py.

lessons.title: Join the Version Bounds
lessons.interactiveContent:
Complete the character that joins the lower and upper bounds.

Make sure to pick ,.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Complete the character that joins the lower and upper bounds.

Make sure to pick requests, followed by >=, and finally ,.

lessons.title: Recall the Package Installer
lessons.interactiveContent:
Complete the command-line tool that starts Python's package installer.

Make sure to pick pip.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Complete the command-line tool that starts Python's package installer.

Make sure to pick pip, followed by install, and finally requests.

lessons.title: Fix the Missing Module
lessons.interactiveContent:
A fresh environment raises ModuleNotFoundError for the third-party package tabulate. Which command installs the missing package?

pip install tabulatepip import tabulatepython install math

pip install tabulate.
lessons.hardModeContent:
You ran pip install math, but tabulate is still missing. Which step targets the package your import actually needs?

pip install tabulatepip import tabulatepip install requirements.txt

Make sure to pick pip install tabulate.

lessons.title: Choose Reproducible Versions
lessons.interactiveContent:
A production report must always use the release it was tested with. Which rule best reduces surprise from later breaking changes?

Pin the tested version with ==Leave the dependency without a versionRequire every version newer than the tested one

Pin the tested version with ==.
lessons.hardModeContent:
You pin the tested release with tabulate==0.8.10. A newer release appears. What does a fresh install from that file request?

The same tested 0.8.10 release.The newer release, because pins only set a minimum.Any release below 1, because the tested version starts with 0.

The same tested 0.8.10 release.

lessons.title: Check the Requirements List
lessons.interactiveContent:
Which line belongs in requirements.txt for a project that uses the installed package requests?

requestsimport requestspip install requests

Make sure to pick requests.
lessons.hardModeContent:
You need requests as a dependency and as a name in your Python code. Which pair belongs in the file and the program?

requirements.txt: requests; script.py: import requests.requirements.txt: import requests; script.py: requests.requirements.txt: pip install requests; script.py: import requests.

requirements.txt: requests; script.py: import requests.

lessons.title: Write a Bounded Range
lessons.interactiveContent:
Complete the range so version 2.30 is allowed while version 3 is excluded.

Make sure to pick >=2.30, followed by ,, and finally <3.
lessons.hardModeContent:
For requests, allow all versions from 2.30 inclusive up to, but not including, 3.

Make sure to pick >=, followed by ,, and finally <.

lessons.title: Install One Package
lessons.interactiveContent:
Complete the package name to install requests.

Make sure to pick requests.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Complete the package name to install requests.

Make sure to pick pip, followed by install, and finally requests.

lessons.title: Update One Dependency
lessons.interactiveContent:
Change only the version number so tabulate uses exact version 0.9.0.

Make sure to type ==.

lessons.title: Explain the -r Option
lessons.interactiveContent:
What does -r do in pip install -r requirements.txt?

It tells pip to read requirements from the fileIt imports the file into Python codeIt removes every installed package

It tells pip to read requirements from the file.
lessons.hardModeContent:
You rename the requirements file to project-packages.txt. Which command still reads its package list?

pip install -r project-packages.txtpip install project-packages.txtimport project-packages.txt

pip install -r project-packages.txt.

lessons.title: Choose Compatible Updates
lessons.interactiveContent:
A project can accept fixes from version 0.8 onward but must stay below version 1. Which rule fits?

tabulate>=0.8,<1tabulate==0.8tabulate>=1

Make sure to pick tabulate>=0.8,<1.
lessons.hardModeContent:
A project can accept fixes from version 0.8 onward but must stay below version 1. Which rule fits?

tabulate>=0.8,<1tabulate==0.8tabulate>=0.8

Make sure to pick tabulate>=0.8,<1.

lessons.title: Audit the Setup Flow
lessons.interactiveContent:
A coworker opens the project in a new environment. Which sequence prepares it correctly?

Run pip install -r requirements.txt, then run code that imports the dependenciesRun the imports first, then create requirements.txtAssume the new environment shares another environment's packages

Run pip install -r requirements.txt, then run code that imports the dependencies.
lessons.hardModeContent:
A coworker copies the source and pinned requirements.txt into a fresh environment.

They run imports immediately, but packages are missing. What was skipped?

Installing from the pinned requirements file before running the imports.Importing requirements.txt into script.py before the other imports.Removing version pins so imports can install the newest packages automatically.

Installing from the pinned requirements file before running the imports.
